title: The Beleaguered Widow
text: Oh! who is it stands in widow'd guise On yon rugged Highland tower, And o'er the wild moor, with longing eyes, Looks forth for England's power? Her Scottish lord untimely slain, And her babe in jeopardy; Her heart is in England's host again, Her hope in its pennons free! Come quickly, come, my father dear; Come quickly, ye barons bold; The Beaumonts' child is a captive here In this dismal mountain hold. Come quickly, come, my youthful liege; 'Tis a daughter of England calls, Whom her husband's murderous foes besiege Within these hated walls. They have slain my brave Athole in yon dark wood, All grim with their stunted pine; And they thirst ev'n now for his young son's blood, Else little I'd reck of mine. Oh! why did I leave the fair land of my birth, For this barren north countrie? Oh! Scotland, Scotland! thou never wert worth One-half thou hast lost to me! Oh! why did I leave my father's hall, In Eamont's peaceful vale, To stem the rude waves of lawless brawl With a lord of the bloody Gael? Oh, Athole! why did thy manly form A spirit so fierce enfold? Oh! why didst thou rush to brave the storm, Nor stay in thy mountain hold? Oh! little didst think of thy sorrowing bride, And less of thine infant heir, When forth to thy fate thou wouldst reckless ride, And leave us here to despair. Hadst thou been beside me, I never had thought Of peril, or famine, or harm; Hadst thou yet lived, I never had sought Redress from another's arm. But thou art laid low! The stately oak Is rent from the clinging rose. My spirit is quench'd, my heart is broke, And I quail before thy foes. Oh, father! remember yon fatal hour I shudder to think on still, When the treacherous Scots from thy leaguer'd tow'r Turned aside the crystal rill! It was hard that feverish thirst to bide Ev'n for stalwart knight like thee; Then harder far for a mourning bride With an infant on her knee! Bethink thee, my father, what 'tis to melt In famine's grasp away; Bethink thee what brave Dalwolsy felt As he wasted day by day! Bethink thee, my father, what scenes and sights There be when a castle's ta'en; When base kernes exult over belted knights, And the living envy the slain! Oh! let me not live to feel and see What my flesh hath crept to hear; If ye come not quickly to save, 'twill be To carry me forth on my bier! Come, father, come, for peril is nigh, The leaguer is closing fast! If thou wouldst not see thy daughter die, Let her hear thy trumpet's blast! Come, quickly come, mine own liege lord, St George! to the rescue! fly! If ever again I hear joyful word, "Twill be England's battle cry!
